_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/db-targets.json (local-only, never committed). devHosts: hosts any client may reach directly (hooks/lib/sql-target.js, which reads only this key) and the only hosts a readOnly:false environment may use - add the compose service names you use as -h. projects: <project> -> root (a path or a list; the longest prefix of -Project or the cwd wins), envFile (optional dotenv file), then one key per environment (local, stg, prod, any name) holding one block per engine: sql (alias sqlserver), postgres, redis. Any string value may embed ${NAME}, also mid-string: it is read from the project's envFile, then the process environment, then the user environment; an unset name stops the run. sql: server host,port; auth (a connection-string fragment) or user + password; encrypt, trustServerCertificate, applicationIntent. postgres: server host:port or url (postgres://user:pwd@host:port/db?sslmode=...; explicit keys win over the url's parts); user, password, sslmode. redis: server host:port, tls, user, password, readOnlyAttested (used only when the server hides its ACL so the probe cannot prove read-only: who verified the access policy, and when). databases: the allowed names (redis: indexes, default 0). clientImage (postgres, redis): the docker route's image. readOnly (environment or engine block, default true): false is honoured only when the host is a dev host and then runs without probe or read filter. Otherwise the probe stops (exit 4, grants listed) on a credential with a write grant until the user accepts and the caller re-runs with -AcceptWriteGrant; it refuses (exit 3) when read-only cannot be proven.
